scope: Version matches are not proof of Coffee Hub exploitability. Deferred findings are not an approved production-risk waiver.

packages.usage_assessment: Installed through vue but no SSR entrypoint is used. Keep the package finding; absence of SSR is a reachability observation, not a blanket waiver.

Browser HTTP client; request configs are constructed by application code. Node proxy/redirect findings are not automatically browser exploits. Prototype-pollution preconditions have not been demonstrated in this app.
Axios Node adapter dependency; browser SPA does not execute the Node redirect adapter.
Axios Node adapter dependency; browser uploads use native FormData.
PostCSS build chain; scanner-prod graph also enters through vue/compiler-sfc. No direct application generator use found.
CSS build chain from Vite and vue/compiler-sfc; no user-supplied CSS/source maps processed by an application API.
Browser login serializes a fixed object of username/password strings. No server-side qs.parse path found.
Vite build tool; build inputs and output paths are repository-controlled. Untrusted plugins or builds require separate assessment.
Compiler/PostCSS source-map build chain; not an application input endpoint.
Development/build dependency. Do not expose the development server to untrusted networks; production serves built static assets.
Browser SPA runtime; no SSR entrypoint. Server-renderer finding propagates to vue in npm audit.

npm.change_scope: Only five transitive patch lines plus required hasown 2.0.2->2.0.4 changed. package.json and Axios/Vue/Vite direct versions did not change. No force, overrides or major upgrade.

python.count_basis: Deduplicated non-withdrawn GHSA records from OSV batch version matches; PYSEC aliases not counted again. Counts are version matches, not confirmed exploitable paths.

reviewed_primary_packages.assessment: Original 0.2.10 is affected. No user-controlled dictionary keys were found entering raw SQL or nested driver parameter values in mounted API paths; original exploitability was not proven and risk was not ruled out. The installed 0.2.12 release removes unsafe escape_dict and passes the driver canary and isolated MySQL regressions.
reviewed_primary_packages.source_verification: PyPI 0.2.12 sdist lacks escape_dict and provides cp312-win_amd64 wheel; SQLAlchemy driver is unchanged. OSV patched-version metadata is stale.

reviewed_primary_packages.assessment: Login form and upload parsing are reachable. Patched known querystring/header/preamble parser findings without changing FastAPI/Starlette. Python >=3.10 is compatible with project Docker 3.11 and venv 3.12.

PNG EXIF parsing via ImageOps.exif_transpose is reachable and remains unresolved. JPEG scaling draft/thumbnail precondition is not used by the current normalizer; no memory-corruption proof was executed. Format/size limits do not eliminate all Pillow findings. Keep image storage disabled for untrusted/production uploads until remediation.

Login uses request form parsing, so unbounded urlencoded parser risk remains independently of multipart patch. FileResponse/StaticFiles routes were not found in the mounted backend. FastAPI 0.119.0 constrains Starlette <0.49.0; do not force an incompatible standalone Starlette upgrade.

JWT decoder explicitly uses algorithms=[ALGORITHM], not a header-derived algorithm or mixed allowlist. Test keys are random HMAC secrets. Production key material and configuration were not read; DER/public-key misuse is not ruled out for deployment. No blanket safe claim.
TLSStream/IDNA certificate-spoofing preconditions require outbound TLS review; no direct TLSStream call in mounted application modules. Indirect SDK exposure remains unverified.
Advisory fixes span 46.0.5/48.0.1/49.0.0/50.0.0. No direct PKCS7, certificate-verification or SECT curve API use in application code; transitive/bundled OpenSSL deployment exposure not ruled out.
No direct P-256 signing call found. Production JWT algorithm is not inspected. Review before enabling ECDSA signing.

python.remaining_scope: Other direct and transitive packages, including optional AI/RAG dependencies, still need individual reachability and remediation review. RAG is not mounted as a first-version API.
